## Why

`torchtitan/rl/` was grouped by technical layer (`components/`, `distributed/`, `model/`, `observability/`, `losses/`) next to flat `controller.py`, `trainer.py` and `generator.py`. Code for one service ended up spread over several of these folders: the generator alone spanned `generator.py`, `distributed/parallelism.py`, `model/vllm_*.py` and `observability/vllm.py`. That left no obvious place for a second inference engine (e.g. SGLang next to vLLM) or a second actor framework (e.g. Ray next to Monarch).

This PR regroups the package by role, so each service's code sits together and engine- or framework-specific code sits in its own subpackage. It also replaces the informal "weight sync" with the push / pull / load `model_state_dict` terms the RL code already uses elsewhere. No behavior changes.

This prepares for splitting `generator.py` (engine calls vs. request dispatch vs. engine-loop thread) in the next PR of the stack.

## What changed

**Layout** (commit 1: moves plus import and path updates only)

| Package | Contents | Moved from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `controller/` | `controller.py`, `work_buffer.py`, `metrics.py`, `WINDOWED_FIFO.md` | `controller.py`, `components/work_buffer.py`, `observability/controller.py` |
| `trainer/` | `trainer.py`, `batcher.py`, `training_sample_builder.py`, `controller_state.py`, `losses/` | `trainer.py`, `components/*`, `components/checkpointer.py`, `losses/` |
| `generator/` | `generator.py`, `parallelism.py` | `generator.py`, `distributed/parallelism.py` |
| `generator/vllm/` | `model_wrapper.py`, `registry.py`, `worker.py`, `stat_logger.py`, attention / GDN / KDA adapters, `batch_invariance.py` | `model/*`, `observability/vllm.py` |
| `rollout/` | adds `data.py`, `recorder.py` | `components/data.py`, `observability/rollout_recorder.py` |
| `routing/` | inter-/intra-generator routing | `distributed/routing/` |
| `actors/monarch/` | Monarch actor wrappers, `torch_elastic.py` | `distributed/monarch_actors/`, `distributed/torch_elastic.py` |
| `_env.py` | process environment defaults | `_runtime.py` |

`components/checkpointer.py` becomes `trainer/controller_state.py` because it only holds the controller state that the trainer checkpoints (`MirroredState`, the state keys). The new package `__init__.py` files re-export nothing, so importing a light module (e.g. `generator.parallelism`) never pulls in vLLM or Monarch.

**Names** (commit 2)

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| generator `pull_model_state_dict(version)` | `load_model_state_dict(version)` |
| `ModelStateDictPullMessage`, `LoopAction.PULL_MODEL_STATE_DICT`, `LoopDecision.pull_version` | `ModelStateDictLoadMessage`, `LoopAction.LOAD_MODEL_STATE_DICT`, `LoopDecision.load_version` |
| `VLLMGenerator.Config.reset_kv_cache_on_weight_sync` | `reset_kv_cache_on_model_state_dict_load` |
| "weight sync" in docs and comments | "model state dict sync" (the whole handoff) or push / pull / load |

The trainer pushes, the router pulls (prefetch on every generator, then load), and the generator loads. The trainer's `push_model_state_dict`, the router's `pull_model_state_dict` and the generator's `prefetch_model_state_dict` keep their names. Metric keys (`timing/weight_sync/*`) are unchanged so existing dashboards keep working.

**Push and pull scheduled in the trainer loop** (commit 4)

`WeightSyncManager` only held the trainer loop's two in-flight tasks (the trainer's push and the generators' pull of the previous step's policy) plus the group-buffer release that keeps new rollouts born fresh. It was a piece of `Controller._trainer_loop`'s scheduling, so it is inlined:

- `_trainer_loop` keeps `push_task` / `pull_task` and awaits each next to the operation it protects: push N-1 before optimizer step N, pull N-1 before push N.
- `Controller._push_model_state_dict` and `_pull_model_state_dict_and_release_groups` wrap the actor calls.
- `WEIGHT_SYNC.md` folds into the `_trainer_loop` docstring and `Trainer.push_model_state_dict` (why staging can overlap forward/backward); `test_weight_sync.py` becomes `test_trainer_loop.py`, which drives the real loop with fake actors.

The actor calls and awaits run in the same order as before; trace spans and metric keys are unchanged.

## User-facing changes

- RL import paths change, e.g. `torchtitan.rl.controller.Controller` -> `torchtitan.rl.controller.controller.Controller` and `torchtitan.rl.distributed.monarch_actors` -> `torchtitan.rl.actors.monarch`. Every in-repo caller is updated.
- `reset_kv_cache_on_weight_sync` is renamed to `reset_kv_cache_on_model_state_dict_load` (recipes updated).
- `torchtitan.rl.distributed.weight_sync.WeightSyncManager` is removed (its scheduling is now in `Controller._trainer_loop`).

## Testing

- `pre-commit run --all-files`: clean for the changed files. Locally, pyrefly also reports 2 errors in `torchtitan/models/common/attention/kda.py`, which this PR does not touch; they come from an older local `attn_gym` without the `autotune` argument that #5358 uses.
- RL CPU unit tests pass on every commit of the stack (441 passed on this PR's head, none failed).
- Every absolute `torchtitan` import and dotted string reference (e.g. `mock.patch` targets) resolves to an existing module and symbol, checked statically. Every `torchtitan.rl` module imports.
- Every RL recipe in `torchtitan_recipes/rl` and `torchtitan_recipes/tests/rl` builds, except a hardware-gated MXFP8 recipe.
- GPU A/B against main (2x GB300, Qwen3 debug model with random init and a deterministic varying reward, so every step changes the weights the generator loads), run on this stack's head (#5317):
  - on-policy, batch-invariant: all 65 non-timing metrics (loss, grad norm, rewards, entropy, trainer-vs-generator logprob diffs, policy age, rollout lengths) are bitwise identical to main, and the stack is bitwise identical run to run;
  - async (`target_offpolicy_steps=3`): differs from main by the same amount main differs from itself (which rollouts finish first depends on timing).

Also included: a separate one-line fix for a malformed call in `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/test_build_model_config.py`. pre-commit's top-level `exclude: 'build'` is an unanchored regex, so it skips every path containing "build" and never formatted that file.

+"""Unit tests for `Controller._trainer_loop`'s model state dict push and pull.
+
+The push and pull of each step's policy overlap the next step's forward/backward.
+These tests run the loop with fake actors (no GPU / Monarch / TorchStore) and check
+the ordering that makes the overlap safe.
+"""
+
+import asyncio
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+from torchtitan.rl.controller.controller import Controller
+
+TRAINER_PUSH_KEY = "timing/weight_sync/trainer_push_model_state_dict"
+GENERATOR_PULL_KEY = "timing/weight_sync/generator_pull_model_state_dict"
+
+
+class _RankValues:
+    """Stands in for a Monarch ValueMesh."""
+
+    def __init__(self, value):
+        self._value = value
+
+    def get(self, rank):
+        return self._value
+
+
+class _Endpoint:
+    """Stands in for a Monarch endpoint; `on_call` runs on each call."""
+
+    def __init__(self, on_call=None):
+        self._on_call = on_call
+
+    async def call(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        if self._on_call is not None:
+            return await self._on_call(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    async def call_one(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        return await self.call(*args, **kwargs)
+
+
+def _controller(events: list[str], *, on_push=None, on_pull=None) -> Controller:
+    """A controller with only the state `_trainer_loop` reads; each actor call appends to `events`."""
+    version = 0
+
+    async def forward_backward(*args):
+        events.append(f"fwd_bwd {version + 1}")
+        return _RankValues({"loss/mean": 1.0})
+
+    async def optim_step(**kwargs):
+        nonlocal version
+        version += 1
+        events.append(f"optim {version}")
+        return _RankValues(SimpleNamespace(policy_version=version, metrics={}))
+
+    async def push():
+        events.append("push start")
+        if on_push is not None:
+            await on_push()
+        events.append("push end")
+
+    async def pull(policy_version):
+        events.append(f"pull {policy_version}")
+        if on_pull is not None:
+            await on_pull()
+
+    async def release_active_groups(count, *, reason):
+        events.append(f"release {count} {reason}")
+
+    controller = object.__new__(Controller)
+    controller.config = SimpleNamespace(
+        async_loop=SimpleNamespace(
+            target_offpolicy_steps=1,
+            max_offpolicy_steps=None,
+            num_prompts_per_train_step=5,
+        )
+    )
+    controller.start_step = 0
+    controller._trainer_policy_version = 0
+    controller.trainer = SimpleNamespace(
+        sync_log_step=_Endpoint(),
+        forward_backward=_Endpoint(forward_backward),
+        optim_step=_Endpoint(optim_step),
+        push_model_state_dict=_Endpoint(push),
+    )
+    controller.generator_router = SimpleNamespace(
+        sync_log_step=_Endpoint(), pull_model_state_dict=_Endpoint(pull)
+    )
+
+    async def sync_log_step(step):
+        pass
+
+    controller._rollouter = SimpleNamespace(
+        sync_log_step=sync_log_step,
+        acknowledge_training_sample_ids=lambda group_ids: None,
+        state_dict=lambda: {},
+    )
+    controller._group_buffer = SimpleNamespace(
+        metrics=lambda: [], release_active_groups=release_active_groups
+    )
+    controller.logged_metrics = []
+    controller.metrics_processor = SimpleNamespace(
+        log=lambda *, step, is_validation, metrics: controller.logged_metrics.append(
+            {metric.key: metric for metric in metrics}
+        )
+    )
+    return controller
+
+
+def _batch_queue(num_batches: int) -> asyncio.Queue:
+    queue: asyncio.Queue = asyncio.Queue()
+    for _ in range(num_batches):
+        queue.put_nowait(
+            SimpleNamespace(
+                microbatches=[],
+                global_loss_token_counts=[1],
+                global_routing_token_counts=None,
+                group_ids=[],
+                min_policy_versions=[0],
+                metrics=[],
+            )
+        )
+    return queue
+
+
+def _run(controller: Controller, *, num_training_steps: int) -> None:
+    asyncio.run(
+        controller._trainer_loop(
+            _batch_queue(num_training_steps), num_training_steps=num_training_steps
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def test_push_then_pull_then_release_after_each_optimizer_step() -> None:
+    events: list[str] = []
+    _run(_controller(events), num_training_steps=2)
+
+    assert events == [
+        "fwd_bwd 1",
+        "optim 1",
+        # Step 1's push -> pull -> release starts in the background ...
+        "fwd_bwd 2",
+        "push start",
+        "push end",
+        "pull 1",
+        "release 5 trained",
+        # ... and lands before step 2's optimizer step.
+        "optim 2",
+        "push start",
+        "push end",
+        "pull 2",
+        "release 5 trained",
+    ]
+
+
+def test_optimizer_step_waits_for_the_previous_push() -> None:
+    async def slow_push():
+        for _ in range(5):
+            await asyncio.sleep(0)
+
+    events: list[str] = []
+    _run(_controller(events, on_push=slow_push), num_training_steps=2)
+
+    # Forward/backward 2 overlaps push 1; optimizer step 2 waits for it to finish.
+    assert events.index("fwd_bwd 2") < events.index("push end")
+    assert events.index("push end") < events.index("optim 2")
+
+
+def test_next_push_waits_for_the_previous_pull() -> None:
+    async def slow_pull():
+        for _ in range(5):
+            await asyncio.sleep(0)
+
+    events: list[str] = []
+    _run(_controller(events, on_pull=slow_pull), num_training_steps=2)
+
+    # Push 2 must not overwrite the TorchStore key while pull 1 reads it.
+    second_push = [i for i, event in enumerate(events) if event == "push start"][1]
+    assert events.index("release 5 trained") < second_push
+
+
+def test_last_push_and_pull_finish_before_the_loop_returns() -> None:
+    events: list[str] = []
+    _run(_controller(events), num_training_steps=1)
+
+    assert events[-3:] == ["push end", "pull 1", "release 5 trained"]
+
+
+def test_push_and_pull_times_are_logged_one_step_late() -> None:
+    controller = _controller([])
+    _run(controller, num_training_steps=2)
+
+    first, second = controller.logged_metrics
+    # Step 1 has no previous push or pull.
+    assert first[TRAINER_PUSH_KEY].value.value == 0.0
+    assert first[GENERATOR_PULL_KEY].value.value == 0.0
+    # Step 2 logs step 1's push and pull, which have run by then.
+    assert second[TRAINER_PUSH_KEY].value.value > 0.0
+    assert second[GENERATOR_PULL_KEY].value.value > 0.0
+
+
+def test_push_failure_fails_the_loop() -> None:
+    async def failing_push():
+        raise RuntimeError("push failed")
+
+    controller = _controller([], on_push=failing_push)
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="push failed"):
+        _run(controller, num_training_steps=2)

-# RL weight synchronization
-
-The controller uses `WeightSyncManager` to publish each optimized trainer
-policy through TorchStore, update the generators, and admit new rollouts only
-after the generator update finishes. Trainer staging and publication for policy
-N overlap forward/backward for step N+1. On each generator, the network prefetch
-can overlap ongoing generation before the local model update. Both overlaps
-preserve the ordering described below.
-
-```text
-Trainer:    forward/backward N
-                |
-Controller: wait for trainer push N-1
-                |
-Trainer:    optimizer N produces policy N
-                |
-Controller: wait for generator update N-1
-                |
-Controller: start asynchronous weight sync N
-                |
-                +--> Trainer: stage policy N
-                |        --> TorchStore: put_state_dict N
-                |        --> Generator: update to policy N
-                |
-                +--> Trainer: forward/backward N+1
-                         --> Controller: wait for trainer push N
-                         --> Trainer: optimizer N+1 produces policy N+1
-                         --> Controller: wait for generator update N
-                         --> Controller: start asynchronous weight sync N+1
-```
-
-## Flow
-
-- Weight sync N and trainer forward/backward N+1 run concurrently.
-- The trainer stages policy N and calls TorchStore `put_state_dict`. The
-  generator update then prefetches policy N into pinned CPU memory and applies
-  it to the GPU model. Prefetch can overlap generation; application happens at
-  a controlled engine boundary.
-- Completing `put_state_dict N` releases `wait_prev_push`, allowing trainer
-  optimizer N+1 to mutate the model.
-- Completing generator update N releases `wait_prev_pull`, allowing the
-  controller to reuse the staging buffers and TorchStore key for weight sync
-  N+1.
-
-## Why the overlap is safe
-
-- The staging stream waits for optimizer step N before copying. It can overlap
-  forward/backward N+1 because forward/backward does not mutate persistent model
-  state.
-- The CUDA-event wait and TorchStore PUT run together in an `asyncio.to_thread`
-  worker. This lets them progress while synchronous forward/backward blocks the
-  trainer actor's event loop.
-- Before optimizer step N+1 can mutate the model, the controller awaits
-  `wait_prev_push()`. The staged snapshot therefore cannot race with a weight
-  update.
-- Before push N+1 can reuse the staging buffers or TorchStore key, the controller
-  awaits `wait_prev_pull()`. New rollouts are admitted only after the generators
-  have applied the updated policy.
